newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals hold 41 pct lead - election poll.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals hold 41 pct lead - election poll.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberal Party has a 41 percent lead heading into the June 2 federal election, a new poll suggested on Wednesday.
The BBS/Toronto Star poll gave the Progressive Conservatives 19 percent and 18 percent to the right-wing Reform Party. The left-wing New Democrats held 18 percent.
The survey was conducted by the polling firm Strategic Council for the Baton Broadcasting System and Toronto Star newspaper.
Strategic polled 1200 people across Canada and the results are accurate within 2.9 percentage points, 95 percent of the time. The results were released on BBS' evening television newscast in Toronto.

In vote-rich Ontario, Canada's most-populous province, the poll gave the Liberals a lead of 55 percent. The Conservatives had 21 percent, followed by Reform at 12 percent and the New Democrats at 11 percent.
In french-speaking Quebec, the Bloc Quebecois and Liberals were tied at 37 percent each. The Conservatives trailed with 23 percent support, the survey said.
The Bloc Quebecois won 54 of Quebec's 75 seats in 1993, enough to form the official opposition in Parliament.

A poll conducted for Reuters by Zogby International and released on Wednesday showed support for Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals falling to 39.7 percent -- below the key 40 percent level for the first time.
In the 1993 election, the Liberals won 177 of the 295 parliamentary seats, with 41 percent of the vote.
The Zogby poll gave the Conservatives 21.5 percent support, the Reform Party 17.5 percent and the New Democrats 9.3 percent.
In Quebec, the Bloc Quebecois was neck and neck with the Liberals and the Conservatives, the Reuters poll showed.
